query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is intended to retain the favorable mechanical performance of the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy while reducing cost and preserving a useful strength–ductility balance. Existing FeNiCrMn research has focused mainly on corrosion rather than dynamic loading. Molecular-dynamics studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys have examined temperature, strain rate, cracking, voids, and compositional variation, demonstrating condition-dependent mechanical responses, but they do not establish how to improve FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading. Given the constraints of remaining Co-free, controlling cost, and retaining balanced strength and ductility, what single intervention could improve the dynamic mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn over a defined range of temperatures and strain rates? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, the causal mechanism, a predicted outcome relative to unmodified FeNiCrMn, its boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy can be improved by adding a small amount of Zr, which will enhance the solid solution strengthening and provide a better strength-ductility balance.
generation.material_initial_state: Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy in its as-cast state
generation.intervention: Adding a small amount of Zr (e.g., 2-3 at.%) to the Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy
generation.conditions: Testing at room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 800°C) with various strain rates (0.001-0.1 s^-1)
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order and its effect on mechanical properties
generation.mechanism: The addition of Zr will enhance the solid solution strengthening, leading to an increase in strength and ductility. The Zr will also affect the short-range order, leading to a more stable and homogeneous microstructure, which will improve the mechanical properties. (Derived from materials-science principles and partially transferable records: PMC10873362, PMC9506522)
generation.predicted_outcome: The Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy with added Zr will exhibit improved strength and ductility, with a strength-ductility balance comparable to or better than the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy.
generation.baseline: The as-cast Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy without Zr additions
generation.boundary: The alloy's microstructure and mechanical properties will be affected by the amount of Zr added and the processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Zr to be added and the optimal processing conditions are uncertain and require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of the Co-free FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy with and without Zr additions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with Zr additions does not exhibit improved strength and ductility compared to the alloy without Zr, the hypothesis is falsified.

Rejuvenation as the origin of planar defects in the CrCoNi medium entropy alloy

Abstract: High or medium- entropy alloys (HEAs/MEAs) are multi-principal element alloys with equal atomic elemental composition, some of which have shown record-breaking mechanical performance. However, the link between short-range order (SRO) and the exceptional mechanical properties of these alloys has remained elusive. The local destruction of SRO by dislocation glide has been predicted to lead to a rejuvenated state with increased entropy and free energy, creating softer zones within the matrix and planar fault boundaries that enhance the ductility, but this has not been verified. Here, we integrate in situ nanomechanical testing with energy-filtered four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) and directly observe the rejuvenation during cyclic mechanical loading in single crystal CrCoNi at room temperature. Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
